A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DreamPRM work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and sufficiently complete for reliable comparison, including material relocated between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, candidate-count scaling experiments, component ablations, and learned-domain-weight analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds original o4-mini evaluations on MathVista, including the scaling curve in Figure 6 and comparisons in Table 5.

M1.justification: The domain-reweighted bi-level optimization, Monte Carlo supervision, MSE objectives, log-odds aggregation, and unrolled optimization remain unchanged. The optimization appendix moves from B to A; evaluating o4-mini does not introduce a documented method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 15 training datasets, MMMU meta dataset, and five evaluation benchmarks: WeMath, MathVista, MathVision, MMVet, and MMStar. The added o4-mini experiments use the existing MathVista task and do not expand dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Figure 4 substantially expands the reported comparator set with a MathVista leaderboard comparison against VL-Rethinker, Step R1-V-Mini, Kimi-k1.6-preview, Kimi-k1.5, Doubao-pro-1.5, Ovis2-34B, OpenAI o1, Llama 4 Maverick, and Vision-R1-7B. These are explicitly plotted leaderboard results. The original Table 1 comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds evaluation with o4-mini (2025-04-16), including candidate counts of 2, 4, 6, and 8 and an eight-CoT comparison in Table 5. The existing experiments retain their dataset sizes, metrics, structural prompt, training objectives, optimizer settings, and iteration budgets.

E4.justification: The cross-model transfer and candidate-count scaling analysis extends from InternVL and GPT-4.1-mini to o4-mini in v3 Figure 6. The three component ablations, training-loss and domain-weight analyses, and worked case study are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the results. v3 checklist item 7 explicitly acknowledges omitting error bars because of resource limitations, but adds no uncertainty estimates or statistical procedure.

E6.justification: New results are concentrated in the MathVista extension: v3 Table 5 reports o4-mini at 80.6%, self-consistency at 81.7%, ORM at 80.8%, Vanilla-PRM at 84.2%, and DreamPRM at 85.2%. Figures 4 and 6 add leaderboard scores and o4-mini scaling results. Tables 1, 3, and 4 retain their earlier values; the additions are results under a new backbone, not improvements to the previously reported configurations.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and objectives in Equations 1–9 and optimizer updates in Equations 10–11 are unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs, and v3 introduces none.

C1.justification: v3 adds an explicit claim in the abstract and introduction that DreamPRM with o4-mini achieves first place on the MathVista leaderboard at 85.2%. The central domain-reweighting contribution, generalization claims, and conclusion remain otherwise unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new o4-mini gains as evidence for effective process-level supervision and more reliable consensus across reasoning chains. Its checklist also explicitly acknowledges the resource-related omission of error bars. The existing limitations concerning fixed domains and expensive Monte Carlo sampling are retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project repository link and revises the reported training hardware from two NVIDIA A100 GPUs to one, while retaining approximately ten hours of training. This is a change in documented resource information; the PDFs do not establish that the experiments were rerun. Other implementation and dataset-processing details are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting the newer leaderboard comparisons and positions its empirical result against those models. The substantive discussion of multimodal reasoning, PRMs, and domain reweighting is retained, with v1 Appendix A moved into v3 Section 2.

P1.justification: v3 moves the full related-work discussion into the main text, consolidates dataset descriptions in Appendix B, and adds a leaderboard subsection, acknowledgments, and conference checklist. Author affiliations and conference information are updated. Most scientific prose remains unchanged, so this is a limited reorganization.

P2.justification: v3 adds the leaderboard bar chart in Figure 4 and the o4-mini comparison in Table 5. The earlier scaling figure gains an o4-mini curve, an expanded vertical range, and revised legend and caption. Existing diagrams, radar charts, ablation tables, and case-study displays are largely retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: The o4-mini scaling curve and within-backbone comparisons in Table 5 strengthen the existing evidence for transferability, while the project link improves access information. These are useful but focused gains on an existing benchmark. Reporting weaknesses limit the improvement: Table 3 still omits o4-mini despite the full-results cross-reference, Appendix D contains a truncated new sentence, and statistical uncertainty remains unreported.
